senses.definition: To remove something from a wall or similar vertical surface to which it is fixed.
senses.example: He took down the picture and replaced it with the framed photograph.

senses.definition: To remove something from a hanging position.
senses.example: We need to take down the curtains to be cleaned.

senses.definition: To remove something from a website.
senses.example: We must take this fake news item down today.

senses.definition: To write down as a note, especially to record something spoken.
senses.example: If you have a pen, you can take down my phone number.

senses.definition: To remove a temporary structure such as scaffolding.
senses.example: When everything else is packed, we can take down the tent.

senses.definition: To lower an item of clothing without removing it.
senses.example: The doctor asked me to take down my trousers.

senses.definition: To arrest someone or to place them in detention.
senses.example: You have been found guilty. Take the prisoner down.
I took down the medicine and soon felt better.

senses.definition: To defeat; to destroy or kill (a person).
senses.example: It took me eight years to get enough on the asshole to try and take him down.

senses.definition: To force one’s opponent off their feet in order to transition from striking to grappling in jujitsu, mixed martial arts, etc.
To collapse or become incapacitated from illness or fatigue.
senses.example: "[…]I mind the year after we came, my father took down with the ague, and things looked dark enough for a while; but, when old Billy Slater, on the Clear Fork killed a fat cow, he loaded a lot of the choicest on to a horse and brought it to us;[…]"
to take the volume down a bit
